title: Symbolic Transformers Discover New Global Lyapunov Stability Functions
whyItMatters: Transformers trained on backward-generated synthetic systems beat state-of-the-art algorithmic solvers 5× over on polynomial stability and discovered new non-polynomial Lyapunov functions.
summary: Researchers at Meta AI and École des Ponts trained sequence-to-sequence transformers on synthetic dynamical systems generated backward from random Lyapunov functions. On unseen random polynomial systems, the models discovered verified global Lyapunov stability functions for 10.1% of systems versus 2.1% for state-of-the-art sum-of-squares solvers—and discovered new Lyapunov functions for 12.7% of non-polynomial systems where no general algorithm exists.
technicalHighlights: Outperformed sum-of-squares algorithmic baselines by nearly 5× (10.1% vs. 2.1%) in discovering unknown global Lyapunov functions.
Discovered explicit, externally verifiable Lyapunov functions for 12.7% of random non-polynomial dynamical systems.
Validated backward synthetic data generation as a general template for neural mathematical discovery.
caveats: Demonstrated primarily on low-dimensional (2–5 equation) synthetic benchmarks rather than high-dimensional open PDE stability conjectures.

scoreRationale.foundational: Tackled a 130-year-old problem in global dynamical stability where no general algorithmic solver exists.
scoreRationale.ripple: Showed compact symbolic transformers can act as explicit conjecture/certificate generators verifiable by classical solvers.
scoreRationale.verification: Published at NeurIPS 2024 with every discovered Lyapunov function explicitly verified via SOS/SMT checks.
scoreRationale.velocity: Demonstrated an immediate 5× jump in automated stability discovery over decades of SOS tooling.

sources.label: Alfarano, Charton & Hayat — Global Lyapunov functions with symbolic transformers (arXiv:2410.08304)
